components.name: DynamicTable
components.summary: Dynamic table. A table people sort, page or act on, built on the table shell: its `footer` and `emptyState` slots, sortable `HeadCell`s in the head row and the shared `TableRow` and `TableCell` parts in the body. - **Data.** `head.cells` is one `{ key, content, isSortable, width, align }` per column; `rows` is `{ key, cells, onClick }` with one `{ key, content }` per column. A column sorts by its cells' `key`. - **Stateful or stateless.** Left alone it holds its own sort and page, seeded by `defaultSortKey`, `defaultSortOrder` and `defaultPage`. Pass `sortKey` and `sortOrder`, or `page`, and the page owns that state: the table reports a press through `onSort` or `onSetPage` and draws only what it is given. With `totalRows`, `rows` is already the current page (paged on a server) and the footer counts against `totalRows`. - **States.** `default`, `empty`, `no results`, `loading`, `refreshing` and `error`. `empty` and `no results` replace the whole table (no head row, footer or pagination) with `EmptyState`; `loading` and `error` keep the head row and swap the body for one message row; `refreshing` keeps the rows at the loading opacity under a spinner. `isLoading` and an empty `rows` choose the state on their own; `state` names one outright (`no results` and `error` are only ever named). - **Selection.** `isSelectable` adds a checkbox column as wide as the row is tall: "Select row N" on each row, "Select all rows" in the head, which is checked when every row on the page is selected and mixed when only some are. A selected row carries `aria-selected` and the selected fill. The keys come back through `onSelectionChange`; pass `selectedRowKeys` to own them. - **Bulk bar.** While rows are selected, the head row becomes the bulk bar: select-all stays in its cell, and one cell across the columns says "N selected" and holds `bulkActions` at the start. The labels cross-fade in place and the row keeps its height. There is no Clear: the checkboxes clear the selection, and the head row comes back when none are left. - **Sticky header and frozen column.** `stickyHeader` pins the head row inside the table's own scroll region, bounded by `maxHeight`. `isFrozen` pins the first column (with the checkboxes, the title column beside them) on an opaque surface, with a stronger divider and the overflow shadow only while the table is scrolled sideways. - **Width.** Under the content minimum the table scrolls sideways instead of squeezing. The first column fills the room and the rest size to their content, unless a head cell sets `width`; `isFixedSize` holds every column to its set width.

props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the file input. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

props.name: description
props.description: Help text inside the field, such as size limits. When omitted, it is built from `acceptedFormats`.

props.name: allowFolders
props.description: Shows the `"Choose files or a folder, or drop them here"` line and enables picking or dropping a folder.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the picker controls and file input and dims the field and its FileItem rows.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Shows the field and its files without a way to choose or remove files.

props.name: validation
props.description: `none` (default) shows no state, `invalid` draws the error state and `valid` the success state. Pair `invalid` or `valid` with `validationMessage`.

props.name: validationMessage
props.description: Message shown under the field for the `invalid` or `valid` state. Not shown when `validation` is `none`.

props.name: buttonText
props.description: The label of the choose-file button when `allowFolders` is false. Defaults to `Choose a file`.

props.name: onDrop

props.name: children
props.description: The uploaded-file list (`FileItem` rows), shown below the drop zone and outside the frame.

components.name: FilterButton
components.summary: Filter button: opens or toggles a filter. It shows the filter's name, an optional count of what is applied, and a chevron when it opens a menu.

props.name: label
props.description: The field the filter narrows, such as "Status". With it the button reads "Status: Upcoming": the label quiet, `text` the value in ink.

props.name: text
props.description: The filter's name, or its value when `label` is set.

props.name: trailingMetric
props.description: The count shown after the name. `0` shows; leave it out to hide it.

props.name: hasChevronDown
props.description: The chevron that says a menu opens.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24.

components.name: FilterMenu
components.summary: Filter menu: several filter categories in a Popup, held until Apply. - **Held until Apply.** Ticking a box changes the menu, not the content. Apply hands the values to `onApply`, closes the menu with a fade, and the content behind swaps in place once. Escape or a click away drops what was ticked; the next open starts from what is applied. - **Reset** clears every box in the menu without applying. Apply then applies the empty set. - **Layout follows the count.** Two or three categories sit side by side at `3-col`; four or more stack, at `3-col` or `4-col`. - **The trigger** is the Filter icon button, its count the number of values applied, on the selected fill once any is. It opens `bottom-end`, the end of the bar where filters sit.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the open menu mounts: an element. Leave it out for the page's overlay layer; name one to keep the menu inside a picture or a scrolling region.

props.name: categories
props.description: The filter categories, in order: `{ id, label, options }`. Options are strings, or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Each category is a list of checkboxes; pick as many as apply.

props.name: value
props.description: The applied values, `{ [categoryId]: value[] }`. Leave it out to let the menu keep its own.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The values applied at first, when `value` is left out.

props.name: onApply
props.description: `(value)`, called on Apply with every category, an empty list for a category with nothing picked. Nothing is called while boxes are ticked.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the menu and the Filter icon button: "Filters", read "Filters, 2 applied" once two are.

props.name: trigger
props.description: A trigger of your own, or `({ isOpen, count }) => node`. Without it the Filter icon button is drawn.

props.name: placement
props.description: `bottom-end` (default) for a trigger at the end of a bar, `bottom-start` for one at its start.

props.name: layout
props.description: Leave it out to follow the count: two or three categories side by side, four or more stacked. Set `stacked` for a few categories with long lists.

props.name: width
props.description: The column step of a stacked menu, `3-col` (default) or `4-col`. A side-by-side menu is always `3-col`.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the menu is open. Leave it out to let the trigger open and close it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens the menu on first render, when `open` is left out.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: `(open)`.

props.name: spacing
props.description: The Filter icon button's spacing: `default` draws 32, `compact` 24.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the popup.

props.name: id
props.description: The popup's id.

components.name: Flag
components.summary: The Popup family's Flag (Figma Pattern/Flag). One surface, 400 wide, padded 16: a 16 icon on the title's first line, the title and its optional description, actions, and the controls. `appearance` alone decides the kind: `normal` is the default flag (overlay surface, a status icon or an avatar, always the dismiss ×, actions as links); every other appearance is bold (its bold fill, no ×, collapsed to its title behind a chevron, actions as buttons).

props.name: id
props.description: Id set on the flag surface.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `normal` (default), `information`, `warning`, `error` or `success`.

props.name: title
props.description: What happened, in a few words.

props.name: children
props.description: An optional description under the title.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions under the description, in the order given, at most two. Links on a default flag, buttons on a bold one. An action with an `href` on a bold flag draws a button that navigates.

props.name: icon
props.description: The default flag's leading icon: a status icon name, or an element such as an Avatar. Unset, the information icon in the subtle icon color. Ignored on a bold flag, which shows its appearance's icon.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Whether a bold flag starts expanded.

props.name: show
props.description: Whether the flag renders. Defaults to true; false renders nothing and stops the auto-close timer.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called with no arguments when the dismiss button is pressed and when the auto-close timer ends. The caller sets `show` to false.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long it stays before closing itself, in ms. 8000 by default; keep it at 8000 or more so a slow reader is not cut off.

props.name: autohide
props.description: Close itself after `delay`. Defaults to true for normal, information and success; warning and error never close themselves.

props.name: timer
props.description: Draws a 4 px countdown bar as the flag's top cap, emptying over `delay`, and steps the corners from 12 to 4. For a timed action such as Undo: the first action undoes, `onDismiss` commits. The bar and the wait pause while the flag is hovered or focused.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class on the flag surface.

props.name: headerClass
props.description: Extra class on the header row that holds the title and timestamp.

props.name: bodyClass
props.description: Extra class on the description container.

props.name: timestamp
props.description: Small text beside the title, such as "11 mins ago".

props.name: sound
props.description: The sound token it plays as it lands, through the app's sound setting, or `false` for none. Unset, an `error` flag plays `error` and every other appearance plays `notify`. Pass `false` when a flag should stay quiet, such as during a session.

props.name: reducedMotion
props.description: Hold reduced motion on or off for this flag. Unset, it follows its FlagGroup, then the person's setting.

props.name: staggerDelayMs
props.description: Optional entrance stagger delay in ms when arriving as part of a burst.

props.name: onExited
props.description: Called once the leaving flag's exit animation finishes and it unmounts.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the flag surface.

components.name: FooterActions
components.summary: FooterActions — 4-track footer layout for Modal, Panel and a multi-step task's footer. Divides the footer into 4 equal tracks separated by `--inline-md`. Every filled action button is cloned at `spacing="spacious"` (48) with `shouldFitContainer`. A leading action hugs the left edge without taking a filled track and is always drawn as a link (`link`, or `danger-link` for a destructive one), and containers up to 400 wide split a single action across the full width via `@container (max-width: 400px)`.

props.name: leadingAction
props.description: Optional leading action hugging the left content edge without taking a filled track. It is drawn as a `link`, or a `danger-link` when it is a `danger` action.

props.name: children
props.description: Filled action buttons placed across the 4 tracks.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the footer grid container.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline style overrides on the footer grid container.

components.name: Frame
components.summary: The Page runs the full height, and meets a docked Sidebar at its 1px edge. - The Frame owns the Sidebar state and hands it to the Sidebar through `SidebarControlContext`. Open, the toggle (`angles-left`) ends the Sidebar's logo row; closed, the Frame draws it (`bars`) at the Page's top left, centered on x 32, and the Page's header row (`header`, the breadcrumb) follows it on the same center line from x 56. - What docks is decided by the layout resolver (`./frameLayout`) from the Frame's own width: from 1024 the Sidebar docks (240, in flow); under 1024 it never docks. - Docked, the Sidebar sits on the sunken fill with a 1px `--ds-border` on its Page-facing edge. Floating (a peek, or opened by hand under 1024) it lies over the Page on `--ds-surface-material-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay` and no Blanket. - Hovering the left edge peeks a closed Sidebar. An outside press, Escape, or the pointer leaving closes the peek. - Either toggle, or Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac), closes a showing Sidebar and opens a closed one; focus follows to the toggle that is left. - Opening a modal closes a floating Sidebar and leaves a docked one alone, and while one is open the Sidebar does not peek. The frame hears it from the shared overlay module (`@/lib/overlay`), so a page does not wire its modals to the frame. A modal opened from inside the floating Sidebar hands focus to the toggle when it closes, since its trigger left with the Sidebar. - The Panel area (`panel`) is the Frame's right-hand area. The resolver docks it beside the Page at a hairline when the content keeps 720, collapsing a default Sidebar first (and restoring it when the Panel closes); otherwise it floats over the Page on the overlay material and shadow, with no Blanket, and a press outside or Escape closes it. Under 1024 it is an overlay capped at 320, and only one overlay is open at a time; under 768 it is full width. As an overlay the Panel is modal: focus moves into it and stays there, the Page and the Sidebar under it are inert, and closing it hands focus back to what opened it. Docked or peeking it is not modal and leaves focus where it is. Its open state, dismissal and focus run on Base UI's `Dialog`, portaled into the Frame's row so a dock or overlay switch never remounts the Panel's content. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640 (never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar) by drag or keys. Width and open state are kept in sessionStorage. A modal leaves it open. Anything inside the Frame opens it through `usePanelControl`. - A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode: its steps are the rows, and the Page's footer holds the task's actions. - Landmarks: the Page is `main`; the Sidebar's `nav` is the navigation; the Panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`. - The Page pads `--page-pad` (24 at every width) and caps its content at `--content-max-width` (1232), centered (`width="full"` lifts the cap, `width="reading"` caps it at 864), on a 12-column grid with a 16 gutter. Children span all 12 columns unless they set `grid-column`.

props.name: areaKey
props.description: Current Sidebar area key: changing it fades the old page out on `appearance.fast`, then fades the new page in on `appearance.default`.

props.name: header
props.description: The Page's header row, 32 high on the logo row's center line: the breadcrumb. While the Sidebar is closed it follows the toggle.

props.name: sidebar
props.description: Sidebar content. Without it there is no Sidebar and no toggle.

props.name: sidebarDocked
props.description: Sets the Sidebar's default request: true opens it, false closes it. Under 1024 it never docks. Unset opens it where it fits.

props.name: panel
props.description: Panel area content, usually a `PanelContainer` and its parts. Without it there is no Panel.

props.name: panelLabel
props.description: The Panel's complementary landmark name, named for its content.

props.name: panelOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Leave unset to let the Frame keep it (and remember it for the tab).

props.name: defaultPanelOpen
props.description: Uncontrolled: whether the Panel starts open when the tab has nothing remembered.

props.name: onPanelOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state whenever the Panel opens or closes.

props.name: panelDefaultWidth
props.description: The width (px) the Panel opens at when the tab has nothing remembered: 320 to 640, default 400.

props.name: panelPeek
props.description: Hovering the Frame's right edge peeks a closed Panel over the Page, with no Blanket. Off by default.

props.name: panelStorageKey
props.description: The sessionStorage key the Panel's width and open state are kept under; null keeps nothing.

props.name: width
props.description: Content type: default caps the grid at 1232, full has no cap (chat, a board, a wide table), reading caps it at 864.

props.name: contentAs
props.description: Element for the content box. `main` by default, the Page's landmark; pass `div` when the page supplies its own `main`.

props.name: surfaceDirect
props.description: Render children straight into the page, with no content box or grid (full-bleed views). The Page itself is then the `main`.

props.name: children
props.description: Content slot

components.name: GenerativeBorder
components.summary: The border that shows the AI is generating content: a 2px rounded stroke in two flat colors, in hard-edged segments that run clockwise around the edge. - **isActive** shows the ring and sets `aria-busy` on the wrapper. Off, the children render inside the wrapper with no ring at all. - **radius** names the radius token the ring follows; match the content it wraps. Defaults to `radius-xxl`. The segments turn slowly while active. The ring is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; `aria-busy` is what says content is changing. Under reduced motion the same segments hold still. Use it only while generating, one ring per piece of content. Do not nest two.

props.name: isActive
props.description: Whether content is being generated. Shows the ring and sets `aria-busy`.

props.name: radius
props.description: The radius token the ring follows. Match the wrapped content.

props.name: children
props.description: The content being generated into.

components.name: Heading
components.summary: A heading's text style, independent of the HTML tag it renders. The tag tracks the ambient level from `HeadingContextProvider`, so moving a heading to a different place in the page never requires touching its `size`.

props.name: as
props.description: Overrides the HTML element the heading renders as.

props.name: size
props.description: The text style. Required: a heading with no size is not a heading.

props.name: color
props.description: Applies inverse text color automatically when the ground is dark.

components.name: Icon
components.summary: One Font Awesome Free glyph, drawn from its name. - **name** is a Free name: regular where Free has a regular weight, solid where it does not. A name that carries its family (`fa-brands fa-slack`) is kept. - **iconStyle** is `regular` or `solid`. Unset, the glyph is regular where Free has a regular and solid where it does not; `regular` falls back to solid the same way. `solid` always draws solid. A name that carries its family ignores it. - **size** is 12, 16 or 24, each bound to its icon size token. Without it the glyph is the small icon size, or the size the component around it sets. - **color** is an icon color role. Without it the glyph takes the color around it. - **label** names the icon for assistive technology. Without it the icon is hidden, so the words beside it carry the meaning.

props.name: name
props.description: A Font Awesome Free name, such as `calendar-days`, or a name with its family.

props.name: iconStyle
props.description: `regular` or `solid`. Unset, regular where Font Awesome Free has a regular and solid where it does not; `regular` falls back to solid where Free has none. Ignored when the name carries its family.

props.name: size
props.description: The size in px, bound to an icon size token. Unset, the glyph is the small icon size, or the size the component around it sets.

props.name: color
props.description: An icon color role. Unset, the glyph takes the color around it.

props.name: label
props.description: An accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: More classes for the glyph, beside the family and name classes.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the glyph.

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: Icon button: a button that is an icon and nothing else. `label` is required because it is the button's accessible name and its tooltip. A filter trigger can add `trailingMetric`, the count of filters applied, drawn after the icon.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Font Awesome Free glyph name (`trash`) or a node.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name and tooltip. Sentence case; name the object acted on ("Edit page").

props.name: trailingMetric
props.description: The count of filters applied, drawn after the icon; the accessible name becomes "Filters, 2 applied". Zero or absent draws no count, and a count above zero draws the selected fill by itself.

props.name: appearance
props.description: The visual style. `default` suits most actions, `subtle` low-emphasis toolbar actions, `primary` the main action and `discovery` something new.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24.

props.name: shape
props.description: Square by default; `circle` is for top navigation.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Marks the button selected and sets `aria-pressed` (leave it unset and the button reports none), except on a menu trigger, which reports `aria-expanded` only. Use it for a toggle such as a list or grid view switch.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Prevents interaction and drops the tooltip and `title`. Leave an action enabled and explain what is missing when it is pressed; disable only while it is sending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a spinner in place of the icon and blocks interaction.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Called with the click event when the button is activated. It does not fire while `isDisabled` or `isLoading` is set.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the button element beside the component's own.

props.name: title
props.description: Sets the native `title` tooltip. Defaults to `label`; `tooltip` or `isTooltipDisabled` suppresses that default.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Overrides the tooltip content shown on hover/focus; defaults to `label` when set.

props.name: isTooltipDisabled
props.description: Suppresses the tooltip and native title entirely.

components.name: Illustration
components.summary: One of the PLUS illustration characters: a textured body with a face, arms and legs in line work. It is decorative unless given a `title`.

props.name: character
props.description: Which character. The first five are the SMART areas; the rest are math characters.

props.name: size
props.description: The frame's width and height in pixels: 48, 96, 160 or 240, or any number. Limbs reach past it.

props.name: title
props.description: Makes the character an image with this name. Without it the character is decorative and hidden.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the character's frame element beside the component's own.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the frame element. They are applied after its width and height, so they can override `size`.

components.name: Image
components.summary: Image: a decorative or meaningful bitmap, with a dark-mode variant swapped in by the browser rather than by script.

props.name: srcDark
props.description: Shown instead of `src` when the OS is in dark mode.

props.name: alt
props.description: `''` (the default) marks the image decorative.

props.name: size
props.description: `fixed` keeps its natural size; `fluid` (the default) scales to its container.

components.name: InlineEdit
components.summary: InlineEdit — text that reads as text and becomes a field when it is pressed. The read view and the edit view are drawn at the same size, so opening the editor does not move anything around it. Enter or leaving the editor confirms; Escape cancels. Confirm and cancel buttons sit under the edit view and can be left off. `validate` can refuse a value with a message, and the editor stays open. The parent holds the value. `defaultValue` is what the edit view starts with each time it opens, and `onConfirm` is where the new value goes. Not for use inside a form: it saves on its own and has no say in the form's submit. Use `Input` there.

props.name: id
props.description: Base id for the edit view's control; the label points at it while editing.

props.name: label
props.description: Shown above both views.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: What the edit view starts with each time it opens. The parent updates it after a confirm.

props.name: readView
props.description: Returns the read view's content. Keep it to plain text: the whole view is one button.

props.name: editView
props.description: Returns the edit view, given `{ id, value, onChange, validation, validationMessage, isSaving }`. `onChange` takes a value or a change event.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called with the value on Enter, on leaving the editor and on the confirm button. Throw or reject to keep the editor open with the error.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called when Escape or the cancel button closes the editor.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Called when the editor opens.

props.name: validate
props.description: Returns a message to refuse the value, or nothing to accept it. May be async.

props.name: keepEditViewOpenOnBlur
props.description: Leaving the editor no longer confirms; only Enter and the confirm button do.

props.name: startWithEditViewOpen
props.description: Opens in the edit view and puts the caret in it.

props.name: hideActionButtons
props.description: Leaves off the confirm and cancel buttons. Enter, Escape and leaving the editor still work.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Field and button height: `default` (40) or `compact` (32).

props.name: readViewFitContainerWidth
props.description: The read view fills its container, so the whole row is one press target.

props.name: editLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears after the read view, naming what pressing does.

components.name: InlineEditableTextfield
components.summary: InlineEditableTextfield — `InlineEdit` with a Text field for its edit view. It reads as the text, or the placeholder when there is none, and opens as the standard text field at the same size. Validation shows under the field through the field's own caption, and a failed `onConfirm` shows there too. With `value` the parent holds the text; without it, the field keeps what was last confirmed.

props.name: label
props.description: Shown above both views and naming the field.

props.name: value

props.name: defaultValue

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the read view when there is no text, and in the field.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called with the new text. Throw or reject to keep the field open with the error.

props.name: validate
props.description: Returns a message to refuse the text, or nothing to accept it. May be async.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Field and button height: `default` (40) or `compact` (32).

components.name: InlineMessage
components.summary: InlineMessage: a compact icon trigger that opens a Popup carrying the full message. Built on Popup so placement, dismissal and focus return are shared with every other popup in the system.

props.name: appearance
props.description: The trigger's icon and tint.

props.name: title

props.name: secondaryText

props.name: placement

props.name: defaultOpen

props.name: children

components.name: Link
components.summary: Link: an inline navigation anchor.

props.description: The destination URL of the anchor. Required.

components.name: LinkIconButton

props.name: label

props.description: One of six appearances

components.name: Modal

A dot that is a button keeps a 24px target, so the gap between buttons widens to fit it. `progress` times the current step: its dot stretches into a bar whose fill tracks `progress`, from 0 to 1, as in a carousel that moves on its own. components.name: Radio
components.summary: Radio — single option within a named radio group. Supports controlled (`isChecked`) and uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`) usage. Built on Base UI's Radio, wrapped in `FieldFrame` (A7) for the label and the description caption. Base UI's Radio has no standalone `checked` prop — selection lives on a `RadioGroup` ancestor. `RadioGroup` renders one real, shared Base UI `RadioGroup` around all of its options and passes each one `grouped`, so the group gets Base UI's native roving-tabindex keyboard nav across options for free, same as `ChoiceGrid`'s radio-type rows. A `Radio` used on its own (no `grouped`, the default) — a lone question, a `ChoiceGrid` cell, or sibling Radios sharing a bare `name` the way the "Group" story composes them — owns a private, single-item group instead, so it stays independently controllable exactly like the native input it replaces. That private group keeps its own `role="radiogroup"` (axe rejects `aria-readonly`/ `aria-required` on a role-less `div`) but drops the `aria-labelledby` it would otherwise inherit from an ambient Fieldset legend it has no business naming itself after.

Hold the rows yourself and filter them (sync), or give `loadResults` for a list on a server (async): it is asked after a short pause, and what it returns goes to `onResults`. On focus with no text it lists `recent` searches; while typing it lists matches grouped by type, then a last "See all" row that acts as a basic search. components.name: Sidebar
components.summary: The PLUS sidebar: the app's navigation, 240 wide, padded 12, on the sunken fill. Every row sits on one grid: rows 32 high from x 12 to 228 with radius 8, a 24 icon slot centered on x 32, the label on x 48, and a trailing slot centered on x 208. By default it fills with the groups for `user` (`sidebarConfig.js`, defaulting to `'tutor'`), the signed-in person's account row, and open tabs from `useOpenTabs()`. Pass `user` and `groups` together to add or override a prototype's own area(s) by `id` while keeping the role's navigation; pass `groups` without `user` (and/or `tabs`) to render custom groups directly. - **Logo row**: the PLUS Logo lockup at height 24, a link to Home, and the sidebar toggle (`angles-left`) on the trailing column. Inside a Frame the toggle comes from the Frame; standalone, pass `onToggle`. - **Groups**: the first has no title (Home, Slack). Every other group has a title row, a full 32 row that collapses its group; an `angle-down` shows after the title on hover and focus and turns right while collapsed. Each person's collapsed sections are remembered in localStorage. - **Locked group**: while `modulesLeft` is above 0, a group marked `lockedDuringOnboarding` shows a lock in the title's caret slot, its rows in the subtlest text with no hover, and the tooltip "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit" (no number). It neither collapses nor opens. - **Training counts**: a row with `training: 'lessons'` shows the Count tag of `lessonsLeft` ("2 assigned lessons left"); `training: 'modules'` shows `modulesLeft` ("3 onboarding modules left"), only while onboarding is in progress. Zero shows nothing. - **Trailing slot**: a count, a dot, the external icon for a link that leaves the app, or a close button. - **Open tabs** (`useOpenTabs()` or `tabs[item.id]`): records a person opened (a session, a student) list under their row on a thread, one line on the icon column whose last row turns into the label column. Each tab shows a live dot at rest and Close on hover, focus and while selected; Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab. Three show, then "Show n more". On hover the row's icon slot turns into a collapse angle and its trailing slot into Close all. Exactly one row is selected: a selected tab takes the fill and its row goes to ink; collapsed, the row takes the fill and shows the tab count. - **Icons**: every row icon is outlined (Font Awesome Free regular) in the one subtle icon color. A selected row shows the fill and the selected icon color, never a solid icon; a brand mark (`fa-brands fa-slack`) is the only exception. - **Inner mode**: pass `inner` and the Sidebar's content swaps for an inner sidebar: one full-width Back button (`onBack`) with the area name centered, an optional full-width context dropdown (`inner.switcher`), then text-only rows (`inner.rows`: a record's stages, or a task's steps). The container, logo row and account row stay still; only the content swaps. The old content leaves at once and the new enters as one block, sliding 12 on `spatial.fast` from the end going in and from the start going back, and fading on `appearance.fast`, with no overshoot. Reduced motion keeps only the fade. Back shows the main Sidebar, where what was left sits as one open row (`tabs`) under its area. - **Account row**: `SidebarAccount`, under a divider. Content is data. Nothing here changes the URL.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A small outlined label that names a category, person, agent or team. It can also act as a link, a toggle or a removable tag, depending on its props.

props.name: children

props.name: color
props.description: A category color: an accent family, on the border (and on the swatch when `swatchBefore` is on). Never a status. On an avatar type the border is neutral and the color fills the avatar; gray agents fill discovery (the AI purple) and gray teams the lightest blue.

props.name: type
props.description: What the tag names. `plain` leads with nothing unless `swatchBefore` or `elemBefore` is set; `person` (round), `agent` (hexagon) and `team` (square) lead with a 16 avatar.

props.name: avatar
props.description: The avatar of a person, agent or team tag: an image source, or a node. Missing or broken, it falls back to initials. Decorative.

props.description: Selectable tags only: a neutral Count tag after the label, such as a filter's result count. Ignored with a warning elsewhere.

props.name: elemBefore
props.description: The leading icon slot, empty by default: an icon in front of the text, for when the icon carries meaning. Plain tags only: an avatar type leads with its avatar. Sits after `swatchBefore` when both are set.

props.name: swatchBefore

Never a raw CSS color. Plain tags only.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Caps the whole tag (default 180). A clipped label ellipsizes and shows its full text as a tooltip.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the tag a link to this address.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description: Router link to render instead of `<a>` for a link tag.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Makes the tag a toggle, true or false: it publishes `aria-pressed` and fires `onClick`. Leave it out for a tag that is not selectable.

props.name: isRemovable

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables this tag. A field disables all of its tags through `TagContext`.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Saving: a spinner replaces the swatch, icon or avatar and the tag ignores presses until it is done.

props.name: isElevated
props.description: For a tag on an image or video: a solid surface fill, no border and the Elevation 2 shadow, with the hue kept on the swatch, when there is one, or the avatar's own fill. Disabled keeps the ground and shadow and turns the content Secondary (Text). Focus on the tag or a link's × has a surface gap inside the ring. Read-only and link tags only; ignored with a warning on removable and selectable ones.

props.name: material
props.description: Colored material for a read-only tag over media or a material surface: a bold or subtle fill with the material edge.

props.name: materialColor
props.description: The color of the material: a status, brand or category identity.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Fires on a selectable tag and on a link.

props.name: onAfterRemoveAction
props.description: Called with the tag's text and the event after the Remove button is pressed. The caller removes the tag.

props.name: removeButtonLabel
props.description: Overrides the Remove button's accessible name. Defaults to `Remove <label>`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class on the tag element.

props.name: id
props.description: Id set on the tag element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline style on the tag element, merged over the `maxWidth` cap.

components.name: TagGroup
components.summary: TagGroup: the wrapper for more than one Tag together. It owns their spacing, wrapping, alignment and disabled state.

props.name: children
props.description: The tags, and any Suggestions offered beside them. Suggestions always sit at the end, after `+n`, and are never counted or hidden; they must be direct children, or components that carry Suggestion's `isSuggestion` marker. `null` and `false` are skipped rather than counted.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's accessible name — what this set of tags is.

props.name: overflow
props.description: `wrap` flows onto more lines; `collapse` keeps one line, shows as many tags as fit, and puts the rest behind `+n`.

props.name: alignment
props.description: `end` lines the tags and the `+n` up on the end edge, for a right-aligned table column.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every Tag and Suggestion in the group, as a disabled field does.

props.name: maxVisible
props.description: `collapse` only: the most tags to show before `+n`, even when more would fit. By default, as many as fit.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: Formats the overflow tag's visible label. Defaults to `+n`; its accessible name starts with that label: "+3 more tags" ("+1 more tag"), or "<label>, 3 more tags" for a custom one.

props.name: onOverflowClick
props.description: Replaces the `+n` menu — for opening a picker or a panel instead.

components.name: TagInput
components.summary: TagInput — a field of Tags with a text entry after them, modeled on Notion's multi-select. Focusing the field opens a list of the options. Typing filters it and highlights the first match; Enter or a click adds the highlighted option. A "Create *text*" row is offered when no option matches the text exactly, ignoring case. It previews the new tag as the Tag it will be, in the random Tag color it will get, and creating reports that color once through `onCreate`. Backspace in an empty entry removes the last tag, and Esc closes the list and clears only the typed text. People can tidy the options where they pick them, as in Notion. With `onRename`, `onDelete` or `onColorChange`, the highlighted row shows a "…" that opens the option's menu: its name, Delete, and Tag's ten colors. With `onReorder`, each row has a handle to drag, or to pick up with Space and move with the arrows. Without these handlers neither appears. Built on the shared parts: `_Field` is the box, `Listbox` the list and its rows, and the tags are Tags in a TagGroup. Without focus the tags collapse into "+n"; with focus they wrap, up to three rows, then scroll.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the field. Give every TagInput one.

props.name: labelMarker
props.description: Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`.

props.name: required
props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

props.name: info
props.description: Text for an info tooltip beside the label.

props.name: caption
props.description: Standing help under the field. A validation message takes its place.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the entry while there are no tags.

props.name: options
props.description: The options the list offers: strings, or objects with `value`, `label` (or `text`) and a Tag `color`. Required; the caller owns the list and adds what `onCreate` reports to it.

props.name: tags
props.description: The picked tags, controlled. Pass `onChange` with it.

props.name: defaultTags
props.description: The picked tags at first, uncontrolled.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws a 40 field and `compact` a 32 one.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every tag and the entry.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the tags with no × and no entry, on the read-only fill.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown under the field, and announced, while `isInvalid` is set.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: The longest a new value can be.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: The most tags the field holds. At the limit, Create hides and the list says so.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: `(tag)`: a tag was added, picked or created.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: `({ value, color })`: a new value was created, with the color it was given. Store both on the option. Return a promise of the stored id to hold the tag on a temporary id, saving, until it resolves; a rejection removes the tag and puts the text back.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: `(index, tag)`: a tag was removed.

props.name: onChange
props.description: `(tags)`: the new list, after any add or remove.

props.name: onRename
props.description: `(value, name)`: an option was renamed from its "…" menu. Store the new name on the option. A picked tag made from it takes the name too.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: `(value)`: an option was deleted from its "…" menu. Remove it from `options`; a picked tag made from it is removed with it.

props.name: onColorChange
props.description: `(value, color)`: an option was given another of Tag's ten colors from its "…" menu. Store it on the option.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: `(fromIndex, toIndex)`: an option was moved by its handle, by drag or by the keyboard. Both are places in `options`; move the option there.

components.summary: Text area — free text over several lines, on `_Field`. The field is 80 high at least, and `rows` grows it from there. With `maxLength`, the caption counts characters on the right. props.name: name

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label above the field. Hide it with `isLabelHidden`.

props.name: labelMarker
props.description: Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the textarea. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Hides the label without removing it.

props.name: info
props.description: Text for an info tooltip beside the label.

props.name: caption
props.description: Standing help under the field. A message takes its place.

props.name: value
props.description: The text. Pass it, with `onChange`, to control the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The text to start with when the field is uncontrolled.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint text shown while the field is empty.

props.name: rows
props.description: Visible lines of text. One row is the short textarea.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` starts at 80 high with 10 corners; `compact` has 8 corners, to sit beside a 32 field.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `subtle` is borderless until hovered or edited, with Save and Cancel while editing.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Dims the field and blocks focus and editing.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Shows the text and keeps it focusable, but it cannot be changed.

props.name: isInvalid
props.description: Draws the error border and sets `aria-invalid`; `errorMessage` says why.

props.name: warningMessage

props.name: successMessage
props.description: Draws the confirmation border.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Limits the length and shows a count on the right of the caption.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Subtle only: called by Save (or Ctrl/⌘+Enter). Throw or reject to keep the field open in `invalid`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the change event on each edit.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called with the focus event when the field gains focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called with the blur event when the field loses focus.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Called with the keydown event. Call `preventDefault` to stop the subtle appearance's own key handling.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the field wrapper beside the component's own.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the field wrapper.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: Text field — a labeled single-line field on `_Field`, 40 high and 32 when `spacing="compact"`. Label, field and caption: the caption shows a message (or standing help) on the left and, when `maxLength` is set, a count on the right. `elemBeforeInput` and `elemAfterInput` fill the slots on either side of the control; a string is a text affix. With `appearance="subtle"`, the field reads as plain text until it is hovered or edited, and saves on blur or Enter through `onSave`. `type="number"` adds steppers after the control. Empty is not 0: an empty field stays empty, and stepping from it starts at 0 (or the nearest bound). A typed value outside `min`/`max` is clamped when the field loses focus, not while it is typed. The field is a text input, so the scroll wheel never changes the value.

props.name: warningMessage

props.name: appearance

props.name: color

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: TimePicker — a time field: type a time, or pick one from the list of the day's times under it (Figma `Time picker`). It is the PLUS Select, searchable: the field is the shared `FieldBox`, the list is the shared `Listbox`, so the box, the list, the keyboard and every state are Select's. There is no separate AM/PM control: each time in the list carries its own period, and typing "2:30p" or "1430" finds it. - **List:** `times`, 24-hour `HH:mm` strings, every half hour by default, shown as "2:30 PM". Typing filters it. - **Typing a time that is not in the list** (`timeIsEditable`, on by default): Enter on the "Create" row reads it — "9:05", "905a", "21:05" — and picks it. Text that is not a real time is refused and the field is marked invalid. - **Value:** a 12-hour string, "02:30 PM", or null once cleared. A 24-hour `value` ("14:30") is accepted and read the same way. Props it does not name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `data-*`) go to the combobox, which is the control a screen reader lands on: TimePicker has no `label` prop, so that is how a caller names it.

props.description: The `id` of the combobox input.

props.name: name
props.description: Submitted with a form, as the 12-hour value.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Defaults to `__ : __`.

props.name: value
props.description: A 12-hour string ("02:30 PM") or a 24-hour one ("14:30").

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: Toggle — turns one setting on or off, and the change takes effect at once. Controlled with `isChecked` or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`. Built on Base UI's Switch: a `role="switch"` span with a hidden checkbox beside it for form submission. `readOnly` blocks the change at the root, so no hand-rolled click guard is needed. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-describedby`) go to the switch root.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the switch, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted.

props.name: name
props.description: Form key sent with the hidden checkbox and reported in `onChange`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text beside the track. Where the label sits elsewhere, leave it out and pass `aria-label`.

props.name: value
props.description: Form value sent when the toggle is on, and reported as `target.value` in `onChange`. Defaults to `on`.

props.name: isChecked
props.description: Controlled on or off state. Pair it with `onChange`; when it is set, `defaultChecked` is ignored.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Starting state of an uncontrolled toggle.

props.name: size
props.description: Track height in pixels: `16` (default) or `20`.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Prevents interaction and dims the toggle.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a spinner while a change is being saved and ignores input.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Shows the state without letting the user switch it.

props.name: onChange

props.name: onFocus

components.name: TreeTable
components.summary: Tree table. Records that nest: a school, its classes, their students. Each level indents one step and keeps every column, so the nested rows can still be read across. Built on the table shell with `HeadCell`s and the shared `TableRow` and `TableCell` parts. - **Data.** `items` is one `{ id, cells, children, hasChildren, count }` per row; `cells` is one `{ content }` per column, and `children` nests the same shape. A row with `hasChildren` and no `children` gets them from `loadChildren(item)`, which returns them or a promise of them; until they arrive a loading message row sits under it, and an empty answer leaves an empty message row. - **Expand and collapse.** The chevron toggles a parent (12 tall in a 24 hit area). `shouldExpandOnClick` lets a press anywhere on the row toggle it too, but never a press on a control inside the row, so use it only on rows without controls. `defaultExpandedIds` seeds the open rows; `expandedIds` with `onExpandedChange` hands them to the page. - **Keyboard.** The WAI-ARIA treegrid pattern in row-focus mode, written here because Base UI has no treegrid part (an ADR-037 exception, like the Select keyboard):  the table is one tab stop; Down and Up move between rows, Home and End to the ends; Right opens a closed parent, then moves to its first child; Left closes an open parent, then moves to the parent row; Enter toggles. Every row carries `aria-level`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and a parent `aria-expanded`.

props.name: head
props.description: One `{ key, content, width, align }` per column

props.name: items
props.description: One `{ id, cells, children, hasChildren, count }` per row

props.name: label
props.description: The treegrid's accessible name.

props.name: loadChildren
props.description: Returns a row's children, or a promise of them, the first time it opens.

props.name: shouldExpandOnClick
props.description: A press anywhere on a parent row toggles it; never a press on a control in the row.

props.name: expandedIds
props.description: The open rows' ids, owned by the page.

props.name: defaultExpandedIds
props.description: The rows open at first when the table holds its own expansion.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with every open row's id when a row opens or closes.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: The message under an open parent with nothing in it.

props.name: size
props.description: Row height: 32, 40 or 48.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the table's wrapper beside the component's own.

props.name: testId
props.description: Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.summary: Text that assistive technology reads and nobody sees: a one-pixel, clipped span taken out of the flow. It is the `.visually-hidden` class `main.scss` defines, which the rest of the system already uses by class name, given a component so the caller never types the class. It paints nothing, so it takes no tokens.

props.name: children
props.description: The text screen readers announce.

props.name: id
props.description: An id other elements can point at with `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby`.

props.name: role
props.description: An ARIA role for the span, such as `status` for a live region.
